fields.description:
## Context
Two test-classification engines — plugins/dso/scripts/runners/bash-runner.sh (sequential) and tests/lib/suite-engine.sh (parallel) — classify tests pass/fail/skip and have repeatedly drifted on RED-marker tolerance, command_hash tracking, scope coverage, and timeout budget; bash-runner.sh mirrors suite-engine's RED-zone logic by hand. Two wrappers delegate to them (plugins/dso/scripts/validate.sh -> bash-runner via test-batched.sh; tests/hooks/run-hook-tests.sh -> suite-engine). Each drift (7225-7708, bf39-4494, e2b6-1059, e8a9-136f) was caught reactively post-merge by validate.sh --ci or CI, never at authoring time (~15% of recent fixes). This epic adds a standing single-oracle equivalence contract.

## Success Criteria
1. Single-oracle corpus under tests/runners/fixtures/ covering passing/RED-marker/skipping axes. Each entry is a fixture file plus a metadata record with shape { id: string; verdict: one of {pass, fail, skip}; harnesses: list of harness names the case applies to (the scope annotation); description: string; drift_ticket: optional string }. The verdict vocabulary {pass, fail, skip} is schema-enforced (unknown tokens rejected loudly). The corpus and schema are documented in a README at tests/runners/fixtures/. This metadata schema is the public contract that downstream corpus contributors conform to (e.g., the planner-mandated runner-equivalence sub-tasks from ab57-b534). The corpus is a protected, hand-curated artifact (auto-remediation epics exclude it).
   Verify-intent: Inspect tests/runners/fixtures/; confirm cases across all three axes each carry a schema-valid metadata record, and a malformed verdict token is rejected.
2. The manifest plugins/dso/config/test-runners.yaml declares each participating harness with its invocation method and a per-harness verdict-extraction adapter; it distinguishes independent engines (bash-runner.sh, suite-engine.sh) from wrappers (validate.sh -> bash-runner via test-batched.sh; run-hook-tests.sh -> suite-engine). The equivalence contract is asserted between the engines; a wrapper is validated as producing its delegate engine's verdict, or scope-annotated out. ("bash-runner engine" in equivalence context = the test-batched.sh --runner=bash composite.)
   Verify-intent: Read the manifest; confirm each engine has an invocation method + adapter and the engine/wrapper distinction is explicit.
3. The equivalence test tests/runners/test-runner-equivalence.sh runs each in-scope engine per corpus case via its declared invocation method (suite-engine direct file args; bash-runner via test-batched.sh --filter), applies the verdict-extraction adapter (mapping engine outcomes including interrupted/timeout to the canonical vocabulary, rejecting unknown tokens loudly), and asserts each in-scope engine produces the oracle verdict (out-of-scope cases report "out of scope"). It uses mktemp for all intermediate state and runs in validate.sh --ci. It completes under 30s local / 60s CI via parallel invocation; if the full corpus cannot meet the pre-commit budget, the pre-commit hook runs a fixed-count fast subset (selected by measured wall-clock) while validate.sh --ci runs the full corpus. The budget is a tested assertion.
   Verify-intent: Run the test against the corpus; confirm each in-scope engine's normalized verdict matches the oracle and total wall-clock is within budget.
4. Pre-commit hook runner-touch-check.sh runs the identical script and hard-blocks commits on divergence; its path filter is derived from the manifest and includes each engine's shared-library dependencies (e.g., tests/lib/) so a shared-lib change cannot bypass the gate; a manifest-declared harness whose path is missing/renamed makes the test FAIL LOUDLY.
   Verify-intent: Stage a divergence-introducing harness edit; confirm the hook blocks the commit; rename a manifest path and confirm a loud failure (not a silent skip).
5. A baseline-equivalence audit is performed before hook activation: the equivalence test is run against current main, every engine divergence is identified and its cause classified (sequential-vs-parallel/TMPDIR contention, RED-zone asymmetry, or genuine logic), and each is either resolved or scope-annotated with rationale, yielding a documented zero-divergence baseline. The authoritative classification semantics (RED-marker tolerance, etc.) are recorded in docs/runners/classification-semantics.md referenced from the manifest; the equivalence test FAILS if that doc is absent. The hard-block hook is activated only after the zero-divergence baseline exists.
   Verify-intent: Confirm the audit and semantics docs exist, the equivalence test is green on main, and the hook is wired only post-baseline.
6. Each cited drift ticket (7225-7708, bf39-4494, e2b6-1059, e8a9-136f) is a regression case whose oracle is the corrected verdict; the pre-fix behavior is captured as a self-contained fixture snapshot under tests/runners/fixtures/regression/ so the case reproduces the historical drift without checking out pre-fix code; all regression cases are green on current main.
   Verify-intent: Run each regression case against its pre-fix snapshot (reproduces drift = red) and against current behavior (green).

## Dependencies
None hard upstream (foundational). ab57-b534 depends_on THIS epic — its G2-M2 planner mandate writes corpus contributions conforming to the SC1 metadata schema.

## Approach
Single-oracle model (chosen over pairwise comparison and per-harness golden snapshots; backed by CommonMark / test262 / SQLLogicTest practice in the recorded RESEARCH_FINDINGS). Each corpus case carries its own canonical verdict; each engine is validated independently against it (O(N), manifest-driven, auto-extends). Per-case scope annotations dissolve the partial-overlap problem (the engines cover different file sets). CI (validate.sh --ci) is the authoritative gate; the pre-commit hook reuses the identical script.

## Scenario Analysis
- Hard-block hook lands before the green baseline exists (critical) — SC5 gates activation on the documented zero-divergence baseline.
- Timeout budget as corpus grows (high) — SC3 parallelism + fast-subset fallback.
- Concurrent tmp-state collision (high) — SC3 mktemp.
- Path filter misses future/shared-lib files (high) — SC4 manifest-derived filter incl. tests/lib/.
- validate.sh integration not atomic on first merge (high) — SC3 integration is part of the deliverable.
- Manifest path missing -> silent skip (high) — SC4 fail-loud.
- Non-canonical verdict string -> permanent false divergence (high) — SC1 schema-enforced vocabulary + SC3 adapter.
- Harnesses emit human-readable, not structured, verdicts (high) — SC2/SC3 per-harness verdict-extraction adapter.
- RED-marker authoritative-source undocumented (high) — SC5 classification-semantics.md.
- Shared-lib change bypasses path filter (high) — SC4 includes shared-lib deps.

## Cross-Epic Interactions
- cf7b-86a9 (platform-parity fixes to the same engines) — SEQUENCING: establish the green baseline AFTER it lands; if in-flight, declare a provisional baseline with platform-specific cases scope-annotated out until it merges.
- a524-fded (migrates/removes harnesses) — COORDINATE: re-validate the baseline if it changes the engines.
- w21-bsnz (legacy-code auto-remediation) — exclusion of tests/runners/fixtures/ is owned by that epic; SC1 marks the corpus protected to support it.
- 2239-1545 (cross-runtime adapter architecture) — coordinate if it matures.
- validate.sh / pre-commit registration peers (188c-47e4, 6add-c1fc, 986e-91c5, 7575-5a90, 1de7-50d4) — coordinate runner-touch-check.sh registration order so the block fires after harness-modifying hooks.

## Implementation Notes
- New files (plugins/dso/config/test-runners.yaml, tests/runners/**, plugins/dso/scripts/runner-touch-check.sh, docs/runners/classification-semantics.md) must be added to the plugin-boundary allowlist before first commit.
- Set the executable bit on runner-touch-check.sh and test-runner-equivalence.sh.

## State Lifecycle
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tests/runners/fixtures/ corpus | this epic | ab57-b534 G2-M2 planner contributions + maintainers | test-runner-equivalence.sh | persists for project lifetime |
| plugins/dso/config/test-runners.yaml manifest | this epic | any contributor adding a harness | test-runner-equivalence.sh + runner-touch-check.sh path filter | persists |
| docs/runners/classification-semantics.md | this epic (SC5) | maintainers on a semantics change | equivalence test (fails if absent) + reviewers | persists |
| runner-touch-check.sh (.pre-commit-config.yaml entry) | this epic | — | pre-commit framework | removed only if the hook is retired |
